subject: mathematics_2a
question_text: If the coefficient of x¹⁰ in the expansion of (ax² + 1/(bx))¹¹ is equal to the coefficient of x⁻¹⁰ in the expansion of (ax − 1/(bx²))¹¹, find the relation between a and b, where a and b are real numbers.

mark_split.label: General term of the first expansion
General term of the second expansion

recall_prompt: Say how you would find the relation — the general term of each expansion, how you pick r to get x¹⁰ and x⁻¹⁰, what the two coefficients are, and how equating them gives ab = −1.
insider_note: Keep ¹¹C₄ and ¹¹C₇ unevaluated — 4 + 7 = 11 makes them equal, so they cancel — and keep the (−1)⁷ from the second bracket. That minus is what makes the answer ab = −1, not ab = 1.

steps.margin_note: First mark. Collect the powers of x: (x²)¹¹⁻ʳ gives x²²⁻²ʳ and (1/x)ʳ gives x⁻ʳ, so the power is 22 − 3r.

common_mistakes: Writing the power of x as 22 − 2r and forgetting the x in the second entry.

steps.label: Find r for x¹⁰
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Set the power equal to 10.

steps.label: Coefficient of x¹⁰
steps.margin_note: Third mark. Put r = 4 into (1) and drop the x.

steps.why: The coefficient is everything in the term except the power of x; keeping ¹¹C₄ symbolic lets it cancel later.
common_mistakes: Evaluating ¹¹C₄ = 330 now and losing the chance to cancel it against ¹¹C₇.

steps.label: General term of the second expansion
steps.margin_note: Fourth mark. The minus sign gives (−1)ʳ; the powers of x are x¹¹⁻ʳ and x⁻²ʳ, so the power is 11 − 3r.

recall.must_convey: That the general term of the second expansion is (−1)ʳ ¹¹Cᵣ a¹¹⁻ʳ b⁻ʳ x¹¹⁻³ʳ.

steps.why: The second bracket has a minus sign and x² in the denominator, so both the sign and the power change; the (−1)ʳ is what will produce the minus in the final relation.

steps.label: Find r for x⁻¹⁰
steps.margin_note: Fifth mark. Set the power equal to −10.

steps.why: A negative power of x is reached by a larger r, because each step of r lowers the power by 3.

steps.label: Coefficient of x⁻¹⁰
steps.margin_note: Sixth mark. r = 7 is odd, so (−1)⁷ = −1.

steps.why: The sign of this coefficient is what the question tests: without it the relation would be ab = 1.

steps.label: Equate and simplify
steps.margin_note: Seventh mark. ¹¹C₄ = ¹¹C₇ because 4 + 7 = 11, so they cancel. Then a³b³ = −1 and, for real a and b, ab = −1.

steps.why: ⁿCᵣ = ⁿCₙ₋ᵣ is what makes the binomial coefficients disappear; the cube root is unique for real numbers, so a³b³ = −1 gives exactly ab = −1.
common_mistakes: Not noticing ¹¹C₄ = ¹¹C₇ and computing 330 = 330 the long way.
